Visible ⲡⲕⲁⲍ requires preceding ⲙ̄- 'of the land' as genitive head; standard Lyc. construction ⲙ̄ⲡⲕⲁⲍ ⲛ̄- 'of the land of...'
Letters ⲃⲩ restored within visible ⲛⲧⲃⲁ-ⲗⲱⲛ; the toponym Babylon stands as the first member of the conventional Manichaean four-kingdoms list, paired with Persia.
Standard pairing with Babylon; 'Persia' completes the first of the four worldly dominions. Lyc. ⲧⲁⲧⲡⲉⲣⲥⲓⲥ for ἡ Περσίς.

Cross-line completion: visible ⲧⲙ̄ + restored ⲁⲍ ends line 6, with ⲥⲛ at start of line 7 forming the ordinal ⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲧⲉ 'the second.' The apparatus gives the full word for context; the actual lacuna at end of line 6 is just ⲁⲍ.
Initial letters at start of line 7 completing the cross-line ordinal ⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲧⲉ begun on line 6; ⲥⲛ + visible -ⲧⲉ.
The Romans are the conventional second of the four Manichaean kingdoms. Lyc. ⲍⲣⲱⲙⲁⲁⲟⲥ for ϩⲣⲱⲙⲁⲓⲟⲥ; double genitive ⲛ̄ⲛ̄- before plural article.
Final ⲧ closing ⲧⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ 'the third'; ordinal complete on this line and matching the 4-fold enumeration.
Copula + 'kingdom' formula at start of line 9, paralleling exactly the structure of lines 7 (ⲧⲉ ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲣⲡⲟ ⲛ̄ⲛ̄ⲍⲣⲱⲙⲁⲁⲟⲥ) and 10-11 (ⲧⲉ ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲣⲡⲟ ⲛ̄ⲥⲓⲗⲉⲱⲥ).
Visible -ⲧⲏⲥ ending; Aksum is the conventional third of the four Manichaean kingdoms. Lyc. ⲛⲉϩⲟⲙⲧⲏⲥ for Ἀξωμῖται with the typical Coptic plural ⲛⲉ-.
Cross-line completion: ⲧⲙⲛⲧ at end of line 10 + ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ at start of line 11 forms ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲣ̄ⲡⲟ 'the kingdom/kingship'; standard formula.
Final letters of ⲛⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ 'those which exist' at end of line 12, with initial ⲟ continued at start of line 13.
Initial ⲟ at start of line 13 completing the cross-line ⲛⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ; visible ⲡ follows.

restoration_note: The teaching enumerates the four worldly kingdoms — Babylon-with-Persia, Rome, Aksum, Sileus — as four parallel states of dominion in the natural mind, none exalted above the others. The Coptic gaps are tightly constrained: each is either (a) a member of the conventional Manichaean four-kingdoms list paired with visible toponym fragments (ⲡⲕⲁⲍ, -ⲗⲱⲛ, -ⲧⲏⲥ, ⲥⲓⲗⲉⲱⲥ), (b) an ordinal (ⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ, ⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲧⲉ, ⲧⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ, ⲧⲙⲁⲍϩⲧⲟⲉ) anchored by parallel structure, or (c) a cross-line continuation of a single word. All thirteen gaps yield high-confidence fills based on the apparatus traces, the parallel enumerative formulae across lines 6/8/10, and the standard Manichaean four-kingdoms tradition. Spiritually, the closing remark 'none exalted above them' marks the limit of every dominion organized within the natural — the Lord's kingdom alone stands above as the King of Glory.
